logic.note: Charge states (trickle, CC, CV, full), output on / off with the low-battery cut-off, the 32 s light-load auto-off and waking by KEY or USB.

timing.note: Auto-off after 32 s of virtual time under 45 mA; the real threshold varies between 45 and 50 mA by module and chip lot.

analog.note: The boost is an ideal 5 V regulator at a fixed 90 % efficiency; the charger is a constant current clamped at 4.2 V like the TP4056 model. No output ripple, no thermal fold-back, no input current limit at 2.1 A.

power.note: Draw from the cell = 5 V x load / (0.9 x cell voltage); no-load current about 1 mA while on, standby not modelled separately.

emulates: Charging a LiPo from USB (CC, then 4.2 V CV, then full)
A 5 V output from a 3.0 to 4.2 V cell
The light-load auto-off (under 45 mA for 32 s) and waking by KEY (press) or USB
doesNotEmulate: The I2C registers of the I2C variant
The four-LED fuel gauge and the flashlight output some boards have
Switching noise on the 5 V rail
testOnRealDevice: Leave it running on battery for a minute with the real load: if the 5 V output switches off, the load is under the auto-off threshold (add a KEY press from a GPIO through 2 kOhm, or use a TP4056 + boost)
Check the charge current on your module (many charge a small cell far too hard)
Feel the board while charging at 2 A: it gets warm
